title: Check a password and wipe it on every path

blocks.text: The page's Q2: a password kept in a `String` stays in memory until the garbage collector reclaims it, and it may be pooled. A `char[]` can be **overwritten as soon as it has been used**, in a `finally` block so that it is cleared on **every** path. Its pitfall 4 adds: a login is logged by user, never with the password.
`Authenticator` (given) has `boolean authenticate(char[] password)`. Write `PasswordLogin.login(user, password, authenticator, log)`:

items: append `"Login attempt for user " + user` to `log`, and nothing else;
afterwards every element of the caller's `password` array is `'\0'`, whether the login succeeded, failed, or `authenticate` threw (the exception reaches the caller).

cases.says: login("alice", secret) asks the authenticator with the typed characters, returns true, and logs only "Login attempt for user alice".
After a successful login the caller's own array holds only '\0'.
After a refused login the array holds only '\0' and the log still names only the user.
When authenticate throws IllegalStateException, the exception reaches the caller and the array holds only '\0'.

concepts: Passwords are kept in a char[] and overwritten in a finally block once used, because a String cannot be cleared.
Sensitive data such as passwords never goes into log messages.
